ing: Gruyère or Emmental cheese 120 g, grated
steps: Preparing the ingredients: Cut the ham into small cubes and grate the cheese, so they're ready for quick cooking.
Beating the eggs: In a bowl, crack the eggs and beat well with the milk, salt and pepper until combined and slightly frothy.
Heating the pan: Put the butter with the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat until the butter melts without burning.
Important: Pour the egg into the pan and immediately lower the heat to very low; the omelet must cook slowly so it stays fluffy and moist, without the base burning.
Adding the filling: As soon as the surface starts to set, scatter the ham and cheese evenly over one half of the omelet.
Folding: With a spatula, fold the other half over the filling, forming a half-moon shape, and continue cooking over low heat for 2-3 more minutes so the cheese melts.
Finishing: Briefly cover the pan with a lid to help the cheese melt fully inside the filling.
Serving: Transfer the omelet to a plate, sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve immediately, hot.
omeleta_zampon_tyri.wine: Pairs well with a cool white Assyrtiko or a glass of fresh orange juice.
omeleta_zampon_tyri.plate: Serve with toasted bread, tomato slices and a seasonal green salad.

steps: Joconde sponge: Whisk the eggs with the almond flour and powdered sugar until light, add the flour and melted butter.
Meringue: Whisk the egg whites with the granulated sugar into a stiff meringue and gently fold it into the almond mixture.
Baking the thin sponge: Spread thinly on a parchment-lined tray and bake at 220°C for 6-8 minutes. Cut into three equal rectangles.
Coffee syrup: Make strong espresso and sweeten it lightly; use it to soak the sponge.
Coffee buttercream: Beat the butter until fluffy and add espresso until it takes on coffee flavor and color.
Chocolate ganache: Heat the cream and pour it over the chocolate, stirring until it becomes a smooth ganache.
Important: Assembly must be done with the layers chilled between each level, so the layers stay straight and clearly defined when the cake is sliced.
Coating and finishing: Cover the surface with a thin layer of ganache, smooth with a spatula, and pipe the signature 'Opéra' lettering with chocolate.
opera_cake.plate: Cut into small rectangles and served with a touch of gold leaf.

steps: Preparing the shanks: Score the outer membrane of each shank in 3-4 places with a knife. Important: without this, the membrane contracts in the heat and curls the meat out of shape.
Dusting with flour: Season the shanks and dust them lightly with flour, shaking off the excess — a thin coat browns beautifully, a thick one turns gluey.
Searing: Sear them in a wide pot with oil and a knob of butter, 4 minutes per side, until well coloured, then remove.
Sofrito: Sauté the finely diced onion, carrot and celery in the same pot for 8 minutes over medium heat until soft and sweet.
Deglazing: Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate almost completely, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Braising: Return the shanks, add the grated tomato and enough stock to come two thirds up the meat, cover and simmer over low heat for 2 hours.
Starting the risotto: Toast the rice in butter in a separate pan for 2 minutes, until the grains turn translucent at the edges.

Cooking the risotto: Add the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before the next. Important: never add cold stock — it stops the cooking and the rice turns chalky.
Adding the saffron: Dissolve the saffron in a little hot stock and stir it in halfway through, for the colour and aroma of Milanese risotto.
Finishing the risotto: After about 18 minutes, off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the parmesan until creamy and glossy.
Gremolata: Mix finely chopped lemon zest, parsley and garlic — this fresh topping cuts through the richness of the dish.
Serving: Plate the risotto, set a shank on top, spoon over its sauce and finish with the gremolata.
osobuco.wine: A Barolo or Barbaresco, or a Greek Xinomavro of good age.
osobuco.plate: Serve on a wide flat plate: risotto underneath, the shank on top with the marrow bone visible, gremolata scattered over.

steps: Important: The cream must be ice cold, straight from the fridge. Warm cream will not hold air, and without air the result is a frozen block rather than ice cream.
Whip the cream on high speed until firm peaks form and the whisk leaves clear tracks.
Fold in the condensed milk in three additions, with a spatula and gentle upward strokes.
Stop as soon as the mixture is uniform. Over-mixing knocks out the air you just whipped in.
Pour into a container, smooth the top and cover the surface directly with cling film so ice crystals cannot form.
Freeze for at least 6 hours. No churning and no stirring is needed — the sugar in the condensed milk keeps it scoopable.
Take it out 5 minutes before serving so it softens just enough to scoop.
pagoto_spitiko.wine: A liqueur, or espresso for an affogato.
pagoto_spitiko.plate: Serve in scoops in a chilled bowl, with chocolate or fruit on top.

steps: Bringing to room temperature: Take the 600g lamb chops out of the refrigerator 20 minutes beforehand, so they cook evenly and don't stay cold in the center.

Marinating: Mix the 3 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, oregano, the 2 cloves of garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper, and rub it over the chops. Let them marinate for 15 minutes so the meat absorbs the aromas. Important: don't marinate too long with lemon, as the acid can toughen the meat.
Hot grill: Heat the grill or pan very well over high heat. The high temperature caramelizes the surface and seals the juices in.
Cooking: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, so they stay pink and juicy inside. Lamb chops dry out easily if overcooked.
Resting: Let the chops rest for 5 minutes before serving, so the juices redistribute and they stay tender.
Serving: Sprinkle with fresh oregano and squeeze a little lemon over them just before serving, which brightens the flavor.
paidakia.plate: On the grill, with roast potatoes.

ing: For serving: strawberry or blueberry coulis
steps: Soak the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla without letting them boil (80°C).
Squeeze out the gelatin and dissolve it into the warm mixture, stirring.
Divide among molds or glasses. Chill for 4+ hours or overnight.
To unmold: dip the mold in hot water for 5 seconds and turn it out.
Serve with fruit coulis.
Choosing the bananas: Use bananas with brown-spotted skins — they are sweeter and mash to a smooth pulp.
Mashing: Mash them thoroughly with a fork until almost no lumps remain, so they blend into the batter rather than forming pockets.
Mixing the wet ingredients: Whisk the mashed banana with the eggs, the milk and the melted butter.
Mixing the dry ingredients: Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt separately.
Combining: Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until incorporated, leaving lumps.
Important: This batter is thicker than plain pancake batter because of the banana. Do not thin it with milk — the thickness is what makes them fluffy.
Resting: Rest for 10 minutes.
Cooking: Cook over medium-low heat. Important: the banana sugars caramelise and burn faster, so a lower heat than usual is essential.
Timing: Wait a little longer than with plain pancakes, about 3 minutes per side, since the thicker batter needs time to cook through.
Serving: Serve warm with banana slices and honey.
pancakes_banana.plate: Serve topped with banana slices and honey or peanut butter.

steps: Preparing the blueberries: Wash the blueberries and dry them very well on kitchen paper.
Important: Wet blueberries burst and bleed purple through the batter, turning the pancakes grey.
Flouring: Toss them in a tablespoon of the measured flour so they stay suspended instead of sinking.
Making the batter: Mix the dry ingredients in one bowl and the wet ones in another, then combine with 10 stirs only.
Resting: Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Important: Do not stir the blueberries into the batter. Instead, drop them onto each pancake after it is in the pan — this keeps them whole and evenly spread.
Cooking: Pour a ladle into the pan over medium heat and scatter 6-8 blueberries over the surface.
Waiting: Cook until bubbles cover the surface and the edges set, about 2 minutes.
Flipping: Flip carefully — the fruit makes them heavier and more fragile than plain pancakes.
Finishing: Cook for 1 minute more and serve at once, while the blueberries are still hot and bursting.
pancakes_myrtila.plate: Serve stacked with fresh blueberries scattered over and maple syrup.

steps: Scoring the skin: Score the skin in a close diamond pattern with a very sharp knife, cutting through the skin but not into the meat. Important: this is what lets the fat escape and the crackling form.
Drying the skin: Pat the skin bone dry and leave the belly uncovered in the fridge overnight. Dry skin crackles; damp skin turns to leather.
Salting: Rub the coarse salt firmly into the scored skin and brush off the excess just before roasting.
Seasoning the meat: Turn it over and rub the meat side with garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, pepper and oil.
Slow roasting: Place it skin-side up in a pan, pour the wine into the bottom of the pan without touching the skin, and roast at 150°C for 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Checking the wine: Top up with a little water if the pan runs dry — the meat must braise gently in steam from below while the skin dries above.
Crackling: Raise the heat to 230°C for the last 20-25 minutes, watching constantly, until the skin puffs and blisters into crackling.
Glazing: Brush the honey over the skin in the last 5 minutes for colour and shine — any earlier and it burns.
Resting: Rest for 15 minutes, then cut with a serrated knife so the crackling shatters cleanly instead of dragging.
panseta_sigopsimeni.wine: A dry Assyrtiko or a lightly oaked white with acidity to cut the fat.
panseta_sigopsimeni.plate: Cut into thick fingers and stand them upright with the crackling on top, next to apple purée or braised greens.

steps: Preparing the eggplant: Cut the eggplants in half lengthwise and salt them. Let them "sweat" for 20 minutes — the salt draws out the bitterness. Rinse, dry, and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until softened.
Scooping out: Once slightly cooled, scoop out the flesh, leaving a 1cm border all around. The scooped-out flesh will go into the meat mixture for flavor.

Meat sauce: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes. Raise the heat, add the ground beef and brown for 8 minutes. Add the finely chopped eggplant flesh, tomato, cinnamon, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until it thickens.
Béchamel: Melt the butter, add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually add the milk, whisking. Cook until it thickens. Remove from the heat, add nutmeg and 2/3 of the cheese.
Filling: Fill the hollowed-out eggplants with the meat mixture. Cover each eggplant with béchamel and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the béchamel turns golden. IMPORTANT: let it set for 5 minutes before serving.
papoutsakia.plate: One or two eggplant halves per plate.

steps: Use cold butter straight from the fridge, cut into cubes.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs, working fast so it does not warm up.
Important: The butter must stay cold. Melted butter makes the pastry hard and greasy instead of crumbly.
Add the sugar, eggs, baking powder, vanilla and zest and bring it together into a dough without kneading it.
Wrap it in cling film and refrigerate for 1 hour. Cold dough rolls out easily and holds its shape in the oven.
Press two thirds of the dough into a tart tin, base and sides, with your fingers.
Spread the jam evenly, leaving a clear margin at the edge so it does not boil over and burn.
Roll the remaining dough into strips and lay them in a lattice over the jam.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes, until the lattice is golden and the jam is bubbling gently.
Important: Let it cool completely before cutting. Hot jam runs everywhere and the slices lose their shape.
pasta_flora.wine: A sweet wine or Greek coffee.
pasta_flora.plate: Cut into diamonds so the lattice shows, and serve at room temperature.

steps: Boil the pasta until al dente (2 minutes less than the package instructions).
Sauté the onion and garlic. Add the ground meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes, salt, pepper, and basil. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Combine the pasta with the sauce and half the cheese.
Spread in a baking pan. Top with the mozzarella and remaining cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until golden on top.
Pasta: Cook in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of the pasta water.
Garlic & shrimp: Sauté the garlic in olive oil for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and sauté for 2 minutes per side. Remove the shrimp.
Sauce: In the same pan, add the canned tomato and red pepper flakes. Simmer for 8-10 minutes. Important: the sauce should thicken sufficiently.
Combining: Add the pasta to the sauce, tossing with a little pasta water if needed. Return the shrimp, and add the crumbled feta and parsley.
Serving: Serve immediately — the feta softens slightly but doesn't fully melt.
pasta_garides_feta.plate: Deep plate with extra feta on top.

steps: Preparing the mushrooms: Clean the 300g mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of water, then slice them. IMPORTANT: don't wash them, as they'll soak up water and end up boiling instead of browning.

Browning the mushrooms: Over high heat with a little olive oil, add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them without stirring too often, until golden, 5-6 minutes, so they caramelize instead of releasing all their liquid.
Deglazing with wine: Add the 60ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 1 minute, scraping the bottom of the pan to gather the flavors.
Cream sauce: Add the 2 finely chopped garlic cloves and thyme, sauté for 30 seconds, then add the 200ml heavy cream. Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g tagliatelle in salted water until slightly firm. Reserve a little cooking water before draining.
Bringing it together: Transfer the tagliatelle to the sauce with a little cooking water and toss. The starchy water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.
Finishing: Off the heat, add the 20g butter and the 50g Parmesan and stir. IMPORTANT: off the heat, so the Parmesan melts creamily and the sauce doesn't split.
pasta_manitaria.plate: A nest of tagliatelle, mushrooms on top, thyme.

steps: Cooking the pasta: Boil salted water and cook the pasta al dente according to the package instructions. Reserve ½ cup of pasta water before draining — it will help bind the sauce.

Pesto: Place the basil, garlic, pine nuts, and cheese in a food processor. Blend, slowly adding the olive oil, until it forms a smooth sauce. Important: don't over-process — the pesto should retain a bit of texture.
Combining: Tip the drained pasta into a bowl. Add the pesto and 2-3 tbsp of pasta water. Toss quickly until evenly coated. The water makes the sauce creamy.
Serving: Divide among plates, drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil, and top with grated cheese and fresh basil. Serve immediately — pesto darkens if left to sit.
pasta_pesto.wine: Dry white wine (Assyrtiko or Sauvignon Blanc).
pasta_pesto.plate: With grated pecorino and fresh basil.

ing: Fresh dill, finely chopped, 1 small bunch
steps: Preparing the salmon: Cut the salmon fillet into medium cubes, removing any bones and skin, and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Sautéing the base: In a wide pan, heat the olive oil with the butter and sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic over low heat until softened, without letting them color.
Cooking the salmon: Add the salmon cubes to the pan and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they change color on the outside, turning them gently so they don't break apart.
Important: Deglaze with the white wine and let the alcohol evaporate completely over high heat for 1-2 minutes; if the wine doesn't evaporate properly, the sauce will keep a bitter, sharp taste.
Making the sauce: Lower the heat, add the cream and stir gently, letting it simmer for 4-5 minutes until it thickens slightly, without boiling hard so it doesn't split.
Boiling the pasta: Meanwhile, boil the pasta in plenty of salted water until al dente, according to the package instructions, and reserve a little of the cooking water.

Combining and serving: Drain the pasta and toss it into the pan with the sauce, adding the fresh dill and a little of the cooking water if needed to loosen it. Stir gently, sprinkle with Parmesan and serve immediately.
pasta_solomos_anithos.wine: A cool, crisp dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, with bright acidity that balances the creamy sauce
pasta_solomos_anithos.plate: Serve in a deep plate, garnished with a little fresh dill and a lemon wedge on the side

steps: Preparing the seafood: Clean the 200g shrimp, the 150g baby squid (cut into rings), and wash the 200g mussels thoroughly, discarding any that are already open. IMPORTANT: pat the shrimp and squid dry with paper towels — moisture prevents browning and makes them release water instead.

Quick searing: In hot olive oil over high heat, sauté the shrimp for just 1 minute and the squid for 1 minute. Remove them immediately. Seafood needs minimal cooking — any longer and it turns rubbery.

Sauce base: In the same pan, add the 3 finely chopped garlic cloves and sauté briefly until fragrant. Deglaze with the 100ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate — this leaves the aroma and acidity without any harshness.

Mussels and tomato: Add the mussels to the sauce and cover for 3-4 minutes until they open. IMPORTANT: discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking — they aren't safe to eat. Add the 200g grated tomato and salt, and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g linguine in salted water until al dente, slightly firm. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining — the starchy water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.

Combining and serving: Add the linguine to the sauce along with all the seafood and toss for 1 minute over high heat with a little cooking water. Add finely chopped parsley and raw olive oil. Serve immediately while hot and fragrant.
pasta_thalassina.plate: Deep plate, seafood on top, parsley.

steps: Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g pasta or penne in plenty of salted water, according to the package time, preferably al dente. Well-salted water seasons the pasta itself.
Reserving water: Before draining, reserve about ½ cup of the cooking water. Important: the starchy cooking water is the secret to thickening the sauce and making it creamy without needing any cream.
Draining: Drain the pasta but don't rinse it, so it keeps the starch that helps the butter and cheese cling to it.
Mixing with butter: Return the pasta to the pot, add the 30g butter and a little of the cooking water, and stir vigorously until the butter melts and turns glossy.
Adding the cheese: Gradually add the 50g grated kefalotyri or Parmesan, stirring constantly, so it melts evenly into a smooth cream instead of clumping.
Serving: Serve immediately with plenty of freshly ground pepper and a little extra cheese on top. The dish is best enjoyed hot while the sauce is still creamy.

ing: Oil for hands and parchment paper
steps: Toasting the sesame seeds: Spread the sesame seeds in a non-stick pan and toast over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant.
Preparing the surface: Line a baking tray or marble surface with parchment paper and brush lightly with oil.
Honey syrup: In a saucepan, combine the honey, sugar and water and boil over medium heat without stirring.

Important: The syrup must reach about 150°C (hard-ball stage) - drop a little into ice water, and if it forms a hard ball, the syrup is ready. If boiled less, the pasteli will stay soft; if boiled more, it will harden and turn bitter.
Mixing: Remove from the heat, immediately add the lemon juice, zest and cinnamon, and stir quickly.
Adding the sesame: Pour the toasted sesame seeds into the hot syrup and stir quickly with a wooden spoon until the mixture is homogeneous.
Spreading: Pour the mixture onto the oiled surface and, using an oiled rolling pin or your oiled palms, spread it into a layer about 1 cm thick before it cools and sets.
Cutting: While still warm, cut it into rectangles or diamonds with a knife; if it hardens too quickly, warm the knife slightly.
Cooling and storing: Let it cool completely at room temperature before peeling it off, and store in an airtight container.
pasteli.plate: Serve cut into small pieces on a platter, accompanied by Greek coffee

steps: Browning the chicken: In a pot with olive oil, brown the 1kg chicken pieces on all sides over high heat. Browning seals in the juices and adds depth to the sauce.
Aromatics: Add the 2 finely chopped onions and the 3 garlic cloves and sauté until softened. Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate, leaving behind a rich aroma.

Spices and tomato: Add the 400g grated tomato, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt and pepper. Important: the sweet spices (cinnamon, cloves, allspice) are the signature note of Corfiot pastitsada — don't leave them out.
Slow cooking: Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 60-70 minutes, until the chicken is very tender and the sauce reduces to a thick, rich red sauce.
Cooking the pasta: Boil the 500g shell pasta in salted water until al dente, so it stays slightly firm and doesn't turn mushy when mixed with the sauce.
Serving: Serve the pasta with the rich sauce and chicken pieces, sprinkled generously with grated kefalograviera cheese.
pastitsada.plate: Classic Corfiot style. With kefalograviera or Parmesan.

steps: Meat sauce: Sauté the finely chopped onion in a little oil until softened, add the 500g ground beef, and sauté until browned. Add the 300g grated tomato and a little cinnamon and simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens. Cinnamon gives pastitsio its characteristic aroma.

Boiling the pasta: Meanwhile, boil the 500g thick pasta in salted water for 9-10 minutes, slightly firm (al dente) so it still has bite. IMPORTANT: don't overcook it, as it will keep cooking in the oven and turn mushy.

Making the béchamel: Melt the 80g butter, add the 4 tbsp flour, and stir for 1-2 minutes to cook the flour. Gradually add the 1 liter milk, whisking constantly so it doesn't lump, until the mixture thickens into a custard.

Finishing the béchamel: Remove from heat and add eggs and part of the kefalotyri, mixing quickly. IMPORTANT: add the eggs only after the béchamel has cooled slightly, otherwise they'll curdle and scramble.

Layering: In a greased baking pan, layer half the pasta, sprinkle with cheese, spread all the meat sauce over it, then the remaining pasta, and finally the béchamel. Sprinkle with the remaining kefalotyri for a golden crust.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 45-50 minutes, until the top is well browned. Let the pastitsio cool for 15-20 minutes before cutting, so it sets and the pieces hold together.

Cutting the potatoes: Peel 3 medium potatoes and cut them into cubes about 1 cm. Even-sized pieces cook at the same rate. If you like, rinse and dry them well to remove excess starch and make them crispier.

Frying the potatoes: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a pan and fry the potatoes over high heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and soft inside. Important: don't stir constantly, so they have time to form a golden crust on the surfaces touching the pan.
Onion (optional): If you like, add 1 chopped onion and sauté for 2 minutes along with the potatoes until soft and sweet, for extra flavor.
Adding the eggs: Lightly beat 3 eggs with a little salt and pour them over the potatoes, lowering the heat to medium.
Setting: Stir gently until the eggs set but remain moist, without drying out. Important: remove from the heat just before they're completely dry, since they keep cooking from the pan's residual heat.
Serving: Sprinkle with oregano, salt, and pepper, and serve hot immediately with fresh bread.
patates_avga.plate: Straight from the pan, with bread.

steps: Cutting the potatoes: Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks. Cut them too small and they disintegrate into the sauce.
Sautéing the onion: Sauté the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, until soft and golden and genuinely sweet.
Adding the paste: Add the garlic and the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, so the paste loses its metallic raw taste.
Sautéing the potatoes: Add the potatoes and turn them in the oil for 3-4 minutes, so their surface seals and they hold their shape.
Adding the tomato: Pour in the grated tomato, the bay leaf and the sugar, and add just enough hot water to barely cover the potatoes.
Simmering: Important: Simmer over low heat without stirring — shake the pot by its handles instead. A spoon breaks the potatoes apart.
Cooking: Cook for about 35 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the sauce has thickened and turned glossy.
Seasoning: Season with salt and pepper towards the end, once the sauce has reduced and its saltiness has concentrated.
Resting: Scatter over the chopped parsley and let it stand for 10 minutes off the heat — like all yiahni dishes it improves as it settles.
patates_giaxni.wine: A light rosé or a fresh white Roditis.
patates_giaxni.plate: Serve in a deep dish with plenty of sauce, feta on the side and bread for dipping.

steps: Cutting the potatoes: Peel the 1kg potatoes and cut into thick wedges of equal size, so they cook evenly. Arrange them in a single layer in a baking pan.
Preparing the marinade: In a bowl, mix the 5 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 2 lemons, the 4 garlic cloves, oregano, salt, pepper and the 150ml stock or water.
Pouring over: Pour the marinade over the potatoes and toss to coat them all over. Important: the liquid should reach about halfway up the potatoes so they cook without drying out.
Roasting: Roast at 180°C for 60-65 minutes. The lemon gives the dish its characteristic bright flavor and the garlic perfumes the dish.
Turning: Halfway through roasting, turn the potatoes once so they brown on both sides.
Finishing: Roast until golden outside, soft inside, and having absorbed almost all the liquid, leaving a thick lemony sauce at the bottom.
patates_lemonates.plate: Pan served straight to the table, with feta and olives.
